nodes.label: Proposition

nodes.statement:
Let $n,r\ge1$ be integers, write $n=\prod_{p\mid n}p^{e_p}$, and set
\[
 D_r(n)=\prod_{p\mid n}p^{\lceil e_p/r\rceil},\qquad
 C_r(n)=\frac{n}{D_r(n)}.
\]
For every integer $s$,
\begin{align}
 \sum_{k=s+1}^{s+n}\left(
 \floor{\frac{k^r}{n}}-\floor{\frac{k^r-1}{n}}\right)&=C_r(n),
 \\
 \prod_{k=s+1}^{s+n}\left(1-2\left(
 \floor{\frac{k^r}{n}}-\floor{\frac{k^r-1}{n}}\right)\right)
 &=(-1)^{C_r(n)}.
\end{align}
For $n>1$, the equality $C_r(n)=n/\rad(n)$ holds exactly when
$r\ge\max_{p\mid n}e_p$; for $n=1$ it holds for every $r\ge1$.
For every $r\ge2$, the product in~\eqref{eq:product-general} equals
$a(n+1)$, independently of $s$.

nodes.statement:
For every $n\geq1$ and $x\in\R_{\geq0}^n$,
\[
 \Dstar(x)=P(x).
\]
Every complete greedy history attains this value, independently of all
tie choices. More generally, if $x^{(0)}=x$ and
$x^{(s+1)}=T_{i_s}x^{(s)}$ describe any complete history, then
\begin{equation}
 C_H(x)-P(x)=\sum_{s=0}^{n-2}\delta_{i_s}(x^{(s)}),
 \qquad \delta_i(x)\geq0,
\end{equation}
where, writing $a=x_i$, $b=x_{i+1}$ and $m=\max(a,b)$,
\begin{align}
\delta_i(x)={}&
\begin{cases}
 \max(x_{i-1},m)-\max(x_{i-1},a),& i>1,\\
 0,&i=1
\end{cases}\notag\\
&+\begin{cases}
 \max(m,x_{i+2})-\max(b,x_{i+2}),&i+1<n,\\
 0,&i+1=n.
\end{cases}
\end{align}
Consequently, a history is optimal if and only if every one of its
merge slacks vanishes.

\sum_k k c(v,v-k)=v!(v-H_v).

These give the first four Heinz formulas of 2 July 2026 in A132393.

A000774 at $v$; A001705 at $v-1$; and A067318 at $v$~\cite{weighted}.
